text: Actions are judged by their intentions.
Know that hearts find peace only in the remembrance of Allah.
Two people who love each other for Allah's sake will be in the shade of the Throne.
If you avoid the major sins you are forbidden, We will cover your lesser sins and admit you to an honourable place.
Prove right the one who thinks well of you.
source: Ali ibn Abi Talib, Nahj al-Balagha
source_display: Ali ibn Abi Talib, Nahj al-Balagha

text: One who strives for the widow and the poor is like one who strives in the way of Allah.
If you are mindful of Allah, He will give you discernment, cover your misdeeds and forgive you.
A servant may speak a word pleasing to Allah without giving it much thought, and Allah raises him by degrees for it.
Ask your Lord for forgiveness; He is ever Forgiving.
Call upon Allah while being certain of His answer.
Look at what is said, not at who said it.
source: Ali ibn Abi Talib, Ghurar al-Hikam
source_display: Ali ibn Abi Talib, Ghurar al-Hikam

text: Whoever leaves showy clothing out of humility, though able to afford it, Allah will clothe on the Day of Judgement with whichever garment of faith he chooses.
The believers are but brothers, so make peace between your brothers.
Do not belittle any good deed, even meeting your brother with a cheerful face.
When a corrupt person brings you news, verify it.
Whoever is given gentleness is given goodness.
Those who fear their Lord unseen will have forgiveness and a great reward.
The one who remembers his Lord and the one who does not are like the living and the dead.
Live among people so that if you die they weep for you, and if you live they long for you.
source: Ali ibn Abi Talib, Nahj al-Balagha
source_display: Ali ibn Abi Talib, Nahj al-Balagha

text: Charity extinguishes sin just as water extinguishes fire.
Be mindful of Allah and speak words that are right.
Say, 'I believe in Allah,' and then stand firm.
When you finish one task, set to the next, and turn to your Lord alone.
Follow a bad deed with a good one to erase it, and treat people with good character.
If you are grateful, I will surely give you more.
None of you truly believes until he wants for his brother what he wants for himself.
Whoever sets himself as a guide for people should begin by teaching himself before teaching others.
source: Ali ibn Abi Talib, Nahj al-Balagha
source_display: Ali ibn Abi Talib, Nahj al-Balagha

text: Take provision; the best provision is mindfulness of Allah.
Whoever relieves a believer of a worldly hardship, Allah will relieve him of a hardship on the Day of Judgement.
Give relatives, the poor and the traveller their due, and do not squander wastefully.
Repay whoever does you a kindness; if you find nothing to repay with, pray for him.
Those who spend their wealth night and day, secretly and openly, have their reward with their Lord.
Whoever follows a path seeking knowledge, Allah makes easy for him a path to Paradise.
The world is three days: yesterday has gone, tomorrow you may not reach, and today is yours, so act in it.
Allah forgives the servant who sins and then says, 'My Lord, forgive me.'
Fulfil your covenants; covenants will be asked about.
What most often admits people to Paradise is mindfulness of Allah and good character.
If you do good, you do good for yourselves.
A Muslim is one from whose tongue and hand other Muslims are safe.
Whoever desires the harvest of the Hereafter, We increase his harvest.
Stay close to your mother; Paradise lies beneath her feet.
Whoever has an inner counsellor within himself, Allah appoints a guardian over him.
source: Ali ibn Abi Talib, Nahj al-Balagha
source_display: Ali ibn Abi Talib, Nahj al-Balagha

text: Let none of you die except while thinking well of Allah.
When you are greeted, respond with a better greeting or return it in kind.
Whoever gives up arguing, even when in the right, has a palace on the edge of Paradise.
Let every soul look to what it has sent ahead for tomorrow.
The believer who recites the Qur'an is like a citron: its scent is pleasant and its taste is good.
Whoever purifies himself does so only for his own good.
Whoever perfects his character has a palace in the highest part of Paradise.
When your brother draws away, draw near; when he is miserly, be generous.
source: Ali ibn Abi Talib, Nahj al-Balagha (counsel to Hasan)
source_display: Ali ibn Abi Talib, Nahj al-Balagha (counsel to Hasan)

text: Each of you is a shepherd, and each of you is responsible for his flock.
Eat and drink, but do not be wasteful.
Ask Allah for pardon and well-being; after certainty of faith, no one is given anything better than well-being.
Whoever is saved from the greed of his own soul, those are the successful.
Even the ant in its hole and the fish in the sea pray for the one who teaches people goodness.
Eat of the good things We have provided you and give thanks to Allah.
In their love, mercy and compassion for one another, the believers are like a single body.
Guard your thoughts, for a thought becomes desire, desire becomes resolve, and resolve becomes action.
The best of you are those with the finest character.
Those who say 'Our Lord is Allah' and then remain steadfast will have no fear, nor will they grieve.
One who, invited by a person of rank and beauty, says 'I fear Allah' will be in the shade of the Throne.
Remember Allah with much remembrance.
Whoever covers a Muslim's fault, Allah will cover his faults on the Day of Judgement.
Never say of anything, 'I will do it tomorrow,' without adding 'if Allah wills.'
Part of the excellence of a person's Islam is leaving what does not concern him.
Whoever sets right what is between him and Allah, Allah sets right what is between him and people.
source: Ali ibn Abi Talib, Nahj al-Balagha
source_display: Ali ibn Abi Talib, Nahj al-Balagha

text: Be content with what Allah has allotted you and you will be the richest of people.
Whoever is mindful of Allah, Allah will make a way out for him.
Keep ties with whoever cuts you off, give to whoever deprives you, and forgive whoever wrongs you.
source_display: Hadith — Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Musnad IV/148

text: Those who strive for Our sake, We will surely guide them to Our paths.
Those who gather to remember Allah are surrounded by angels, covered by mercy, and tranquillity descends upon them.
Be patient; your patience is only through Allah.
Ten rewards are written for whoever says 'Peace be upon you.'
Whoever looks at his own faults has no time for the faults of others.
source: Ali ibn Abi Talib, Nahj al-Balagha
source_display: Ali ibn Abi Talib, Nahj al-Balagha

text: Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good counsel.
Know Allah in times of ease, and He will know you in times of hardship.
source_display: Hadith — Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Musnad I/307

text: When you speak, speak justly, even if it concerns a relative.
The deeds most beloved to Allah are those done consistently, even if small.
Whoever believes in Allah, He guides his heart.
A person follows the way of his close friend, so be careful whom you befriend.
An hour of reflection is better than a night of worship.
Whoever eases things for someone in difficulty, Allah will ease things for him in this world and the next.
Call upon your Lord humbly and in secret.
Mention the good deeds of your dead and refrain from mentioning their faults.
Establish prayer, enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, and be patient with what befalls you.
Beware the prayer of the oppressed, for there is no veil between it and Allah.
Those who obey Allah and His Messenger, fear Allah and are mindful of Him, they are the truly successful.
Whoever does not thank people does not thank Allah.
When you hear a report, grasp it to understand it, not merely to relay it.
source: Ali ibn Abi Talib, Nahj al-Balagha
source_display: Ali ibn Abi Talib, Nahj al-Balagha

text: Whoever says 'Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him' a hundred times a day, his sins are forgiven even if they are like the foam of the sea.
Let there be among you a community that calls to good, enjoins what is right and forbids what is wrong.
Nothing will be heavier on the believer's scale on the Day of Judgement than good character.
Do not turn your cheek away from people in arrogance.
The wise person is one who holds himself to account and works for what comes after death.
Good words rise up to Him, and righteous deeds He raises.
The better of two estranged brothers is the one who greets first.
Hearts have times of eagerness and times of turning away; when eager, hold them to voluntary devotions, and when turning away, keep them to the obligations.
source: Ali ibn Abi Talib, Nahj al-Balagha
source_display: Ali ibn Abi Talib, Nahj al-Balagha

text: Whoever shows mercy, even to a sparrow, Allah will show him mercy on the Day of Judgement.
Do good; indeed Allah loves those who do good.
Whoever intends a bad deed but refrains from it for Allah's sake, Allah records for him a complete good deed.
Let no people mock another people; perhaps they are better than them.
The best of neighbours in Allah's sight is the one best to his neighbour.
Whoever hopes to meet his Lord, let him do righteous deeds.
Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him maintain ties of kinship.
Do not be the slave of another; Allah has created you free.
source: Ali ibn Abi Talib, Nahj al-Balagha (counsel to Hasan)
source_display: Ali ibn Abi Talib, Nahj al-Balagha (counsel to Hasan)

text: Worship Allah as if you see Him; for though you do not see Him, He sees you.
Whoever comes with a good deed will have ten times its like.
Allah shows mercy only to those of His servants who are merciful.
Remember your Lord within yourself, humbly and with awe, softly, morning and evening, and do not be among the heedless.
Take on the deeds you are able to sustain; Allah does not tire until you tire.
Speak good words to people.
Be mindful of Allah and He will protect you; when you ask, ask Allah, and when you seek help, seek it from Allah.
Let not the delay of the gift, despite your persistence in prayer, make you despair.
Saying 'Praise be to Allah' fills the scale.
Whoever saves a life, it is as if he saved the life of all mankind.
A youth who grows up in the worship of his Lord will be in the shade of the Throne.
Do not nullify your charity with reminders and hurt.
Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak good or remain silent.
Overlook with gracious forgiveness.
One who remembers Allah in solitude and his eyes overflow will be in the shade of the Throne.
Look at the traces of Allah's mercy: how He gives life to the earth after its death!
When buyer and seller speak truthfully and disclose defects, their transaction is blessed.
If you do not occupy your soul with truth, it will occupy you with falsehood.
Whoever builds a mosque for Allah's sake, Allah builds for him its like in Paradise.
If you give charity openly, that is good; but if you conceal it and give it to the poor, that is better for you.
The nearest of people to Allah is the one who greets first.
Let not your wealth or your children divert you from the remembrance of Allah.
The deed most beloved to Allah is bringing joy into a Muslim's heart.
Be patient; Allah does not let the reward of those who do good go to waste.
The truthful, trustworthy merchant is with the prophets, the truthful and the martyrs.
Reflection calls a person to goodness and to acting upon it.
Help your brother whether he is wronged or doing wrong; helping the wrongdoer means stopping him from wrongdoing.
Man will have nothing but what he strives for.
Your smile to your brother is a charity for you.
Remember Me, and I will remember you.
Recite the Qur'an, for it will come on the Day of Judgement as an intercessor for its companions.
Give full measure when you measure and weigh with an even balance; that is better and best in outcome.
A good companion and a bad one are like the carrier of musk and the blower of the bellows.
When the believer is silent he reflects, when he looks he takes heed, and when he speaks he remembers Allah.
Do not oppress the orphan, do not turn away the one who asks, and speak of your Lord's blessings with gratitude.
If your good deeds please you and your bad deeds grieve you, you are a believer.
source: al-Tirmidhi 2165; Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Musnad V/251
source_display: Hadith — al-Tirmidhi 2165; Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Musnad V/251

text: Allah loves those who act justly.
Do not speak much without remembering Allah, for much talk without remembrance hardens the heart.
Do not abandon remembrance because you are not present with Allah in it; heedlessness without it is worse than heedlessness within it.
Treat your children fairly.
Whoever purifies the soul has truly succeeded.
Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him be good to his neighbour.
When a prompting from Satan touches the mindful, they remember Allah and at once see clearly.
Be truthful when you speak, fulfil your promises, and return what is entrusted to you.
source_display: Hadith — Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Musnad V/323

text: Repel evil with that which is best.
Charity given in secret extinguishes the Lord's anger.
Learn knowledge, and learn with it dignity and tranquillity.
By good character a believer attains the rank of one who fasts by day and prays by night.
Whoever does righteous deeds as a believer, We will surely grant him a good life.
The fire will not touch an eye that wept out of awe of Allah.
Be moderate in your walk and lower your voice.
Whoever spends in the way of Allah, seven hundredfold is recorded for him.
Stand firm as you have been commanded.
The strong one is the one who controls himself when angry.
Allah does not change the condition of a people until they change what is within themselves.
Whoever loves his brother for Allah's sake, Allah loves him.
Do not think ill of a word from your brother while you can find a good meaning for it.
Whoever intends a good deed but cannot do it, Allah records for him a complete good deed.
Do not walk on the earth arrogantly; you cannot split the earth, nor reach the mountains in height.
Allah increases the honour of a servant who forgives.
Worship your Lord and do good, so that you may succeed.
The best of you are those who learn the Qur'an and teach it.
Indeed, Allah commands justice, excellence and giving to relatives.
Whoever seeks Allah's pleasure even at the cost of people's displeasure, Allah is pleased with him and makes people pleased with him.
There is a disarray in the heart that nothing gathers except turning to Allah.
Every prostration made for Allah raises a servant by a degree and removes a sin.
The good end belongs to those who are mindful of Allah.
An angel says 'How good was your walk' to one who visits a brother for Allah's sake.
When you are told to make room in gatherings, make room, and Allah will make room for you.
Blessed is the one who is a key to good and a lock against evil.
The most honoured of you in Allah's sight is the most mindful of Him.
Consult your heart: righteousness is what the soul feels at peace with.
Do not say what you do not know; indeed, do not say all that you know.
source: Ali ibn Abi Talib, Nahj al-Balagha
source_display: Ali ibn Abi Talib, Nahj al-Balagha

text: Keep to the middle way, keep to the middle way, and you will reach your goal.
Whoever does righteous deeds as a believer, his effort will not be denied.
Whoever visits a sick person remains in the garden of Paradise until he returns.
Turn to Allah in sincere repentance.
Guard against the forbidden and you will be the most devoted of people.
Hold to forgiveness, enjoin what is good, and turn away from the ignorant.
Give the worker his wage before his sweat dries.
When asked about what you do not know, do not be ashamed to say 'I do not know.'
source: Ali ibn Abi Talib, Nahj al-Balagha
source_display: Ali ibn Abi Talib, Nahj al-Balagha

text: Those who are patient will be given their reward without measure.
Allah accepts only deeds done sincerely, seeking His pleasure.
Successful indeed is the one who purifies himself, remembers his Lord's name and prays.
Gentleness beautifies whatever it is in.
Do good just as you would love good to be done to you.
source: Ali ibn Abi Talib, Nahj al-Balagha (counsel to Hasan)
source_display: Ali ibn Abi Talib, Nahj al-Balagha (counsel to Hasan)

text: Show mercy and you will be shown mercy; forgive and you will be forgiven.
source_display: Hadith — Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Musnad II/165

text: Seek help through patience and prayer.
A Muslim is a Muslim's brother; he does not wrong him nor abandon him.
Whatever good you send ahead for yourselves, you will find it with Allah.
Ask Allah for beneficial knowledge and seek refuge in Him from knowledge that does not benefit.
For those who believe and do righteous deeds, the Most Merciful will create affection.
Whoever restrains his anger while able to act on it, Allah will call him before all creation and honour him.
Be patient with a beautiful patience.
If you relied on Allah as you should, He would provide for you as He provides for the birds.
The believer thinks well of his Lord and so does his deeds well.
There is a reward in kindness to every living being.
Let not hatred of a people lead you to be unjust.
Reflect upon Allah's creation, and do not delve into His essence.
Do good as Allah has done good to you.
Whenever a servant is patient with a wrong done to him, Allah increases his honour.
Give glad tidings to My servants who listen to what is said and follow the best of it.
Whoever makes the Hereafter his concern, Allah places richness in his heart and gathers his scattered affairs.
Do not keep company with one whose state does not uplift you and whose words do not lead you to Allah.
Whoever mentions a favour done to him has thanked for it.
Those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah are like a seed that grows seven ears, each with a hundred grains.
Allah loves that when one of you does a job, he does it well and with excellence.
Good deeds remove bad deeds.
Bringing justice between two people is a charity.
Whoever is mindful of Allah, Allah makes his affairs easy for him.
Whoever wishes his provision expanded and his life blessed, let him maintain family ties.
When you gain power over your enemy, make forgiving him your thanks for that power.
source: Ali ibn Abi Talib, Nahj al-Balagha
source_display: Ali ibn Abi Talib, Nahj al-Balagha

text: Whoever fulfils his brother's need, Allah fulfils his need.
If you lend Allah a goodly loan, He will multiply it for you and forgive you.
Make things easy, not difficult; give glad tidings, do not drive people away.
Be grateful to Allah; whoever is grateful is grateful for his own good.
One who gives charity so secretly that his left hand does not know what his right hand gives will be in the shade of the Throne.
Whoever repents and does righteous deeds has truly turned to Allah.
Whoever brings his need to Allah, Allah will soon provide for him.
If you hear an unpleasant word from your brother, seek one to seventy excuses for him.
I and the one who cares for an orphan will be in Paradise like these two fingers.
Whoever fulfils his covenant and is mindful of Allah, Allah loves the mindful.
Be in this world as though you were a stranger or a traveller.
Remember the name of your Lord and devote yourself to Him completely.
In the body there is a piece of flesh; if it is sound, the whole body is sound. Indeed, it is the heart.
Whoever submits himself to Allah while doing good has grasped the most firm handhold.
Guiding someone who cannot see is a charity for you.
Make yourself the measure between you and others; love for others what you love for yourself.
source: Ali ibn Abi Talib, Nahj al-Balagha (counsel to Hasan)
source_display: Ali ibn Abi Talib, Nahj al-Balagha (counsel to Hasan)

text: Zakat given seeking Allah's pleasure, those who give it are the ones whose reward is multiplied.
There are two blessings in which many people are deceived: health and free time.
Seek of Allah's bounty, and remember Allah often so that you may succeed.
If you want your heart to soften, feed the poor and stroke the orphan's head.
source_display: Hadith — Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Musnad II/263

text: Cooperate in righteousness and piety, not in sin and aggression.
Charity does not decrease wealth, and Allah raises whoever is humble for His sake.
Let none of you hope in anyone but his Lord, nor fear anything but his own sin.
source: Ali ibn Abi Talib, Nahj al-Balagha
source_display: Ali ibn Abi Talib, Nahj al-Balagha

text: When you pray for your brother in his absence, an angel says, 'And for you the same.'
Be patient for the sake of your Lord.
Be detached from the world and Allah will love you; do not covet what people have and people will love you.
Give of the good things you have earned and of what We bring forth for you from the earth.
The servant is nearest to his Lord when prostrating, so increase your supplication then.
Once you have decided, put your trust in Allah; Allah loves those who trust in Him.
Two Muslims who meet and shake hands are forgiven before they part.
Whoever reforms his inner self, Allah reforms his outer self.
source: Ali ibn Abi Talib, Nahj al-Balagha
source_display: Ali ibn Abi Talib, Nahj al-Balagha

text: Whoever goes out seeking knowledge is in the way of Allah until he returns.
Whoever intercedes for a good cause will have a share of it.
Allah loves forbearance and deliberation.
If you pardon, overlook and forgive, then Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
Give gifts to one another, and you will love one another.
The servants of the Most Merciful walk upon the earth with dignity, and when the ignorant address them, they say 'Peace.'
If you give something up for Allah's sake, Allah will replace it with something better.
source_display: Hadith — Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Musnad V/363

text: Opportunity passes like a cloud; seize the opportunities for good.
source: Ali ibn Abi Talib, Nahj al-Balagha
source_display: Ali ibn Abi Talib, Nahj al-Balagha

text: Guiding someone who has lost his way is a charity for you.
Your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him and be good to your parents.
Allah is pleased with the servant who praises Him for each morsel he eats and each sip he drinks.
Do not despair of Allah's mercy; Allah forgives all sins.
Allah loves the servant who is mindful, content at heart and inconspicuous.
Allah is with those who are mindful and those who do good.
One who guides to good is like one who does it.
If you must part from your brother, leave room in your heart for him to return.
source: Ali ibn Abi Talib, Nahj al-Balagha (counsel to Hasan)
source_display: Ali ibn Abi Talib, Nahj al-Balagha (counsel to Hasan)

text: Whoever gives in charity the equivalent of a date from lawful earnings, Allah nurtures it until it becomes like a mountain.
Blessed are those who believe and do righteous deeds.
For whoever says 'Glory be to Allah the Magnificent, and praise be to Him,' a palm tree is planted in Paradise.
Do not mix truth with falsehood, nor conceal the truth knowingly.
If a Muslim plants a tree and a creature eats from it, it is charity for him.
Whoever forgives and makes reconciliation, his reward is with Allah.
Your prayer is answered as long as you do not hasten, saying 'I prayed but was not answered.'
You are but days; whenever a day passes, a part of you passes.
Whoever defends his brother's honour, Allah will shield his face from the Fire on the Day of Judgement.
Those who spend in the way of Allah without following it with reminders or hurt have their reward with their Lord.
Whoever gives a fasting person food to break his fast earns the same reward as him.
Keep yourself patiently with those who call on their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance.
Allah loves lofty and noble matters and dislikes the petty ones.
We will surely reward those who are patient according to the best of what they used to do.
Allah does not look at your forms and wealth, but at your hearts and deeds.
Two units of prayer offered with reflection are better than a whole night of worship with a heedless heart.
You will never attain righteousness until you spend from what you love.
The best of you are those who are best to their families.
Glorify your Lord with praise whenever you rise.
If the Hour comes while one of you holds a sapling, let him plant it if he can.
source_display: Hadith — Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Musnad III/191

text: If you support Allah, He will support you and make your steps firm.
All the children of Adam err, and the best of those who err are those who repent.
Do not be ashamed of giving little, for refusing is even less.
source: Ali ibn Abi Talib, Nahj al-Balagha
source_display: Ali ibn Abi Talib, Nahj al-Balagha

text: Be humble, so that no one boasts over another and no one wrongs another.
Forgiving is closer to piety; do not forget graciousness among yourselves.
My servant keeps drawing near to Me with voluntary deeds after the obligatory, until I love him.
Allah loves those who are patient.
One who repents from sin is like one who has no sin.
Do not covet what Allah has favoured some of you with over others.
Whoever gives respite to a debtor in hardship or forgives his debt, Allah will shade him in His shade.
Do not wrong others, just as you would not like to be wronged.
source: Ali ibn Abi Talib, Nahj al-Balagha (counsel to Hasan)
source_display: Ali ibn Abi Talib, Nahj al-Balagha (counsel to Hasan)

text: You are rewarded for everything you spend for Allah's sake, even the morsel you put in your spouse's mouth.
Allah's mercy is near to those who do good.
Whoever tries to be patient, Allah grants him patience; no one is given a gift better or vaster than patience.
Be mindful of Allah and be with the truthful.
The best of people are those most beneficial to people.
Do not approach indecencies, whether open or hidden.
Greet everyone with peace, whether you know them or not.
Night and day are working on you, so work in them.
Value your life before death, your health before illness and your free time before busyness.
Be patient and outdo others in endurance.
Let your tongue remain moist with the remembrance of Allah.
The mindful spend in ease and hardship, restrain their anger and pardon people.
The Fire is forbidden to one who is easygoing, gentle and close to people.
For those who do good there is the best reward and even more.
Strive for what benefits you, seek help from Allah, and do not give up.
Hold yourselves to account before you are held to account.
If one of you loves his brother, let him tell him that he loves him.
Prostrate and draw near.
The believer is grateful in joy and patient in hardship; both states are good for him.
Do not pursue what you have no knowledge of; hearing, sight and heart will all be questioned.
Whoever abandons lying, even in jest, has a palace in the middle of Paradise.
Whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it.
Allah helps a servant as long as the servant helps his brother.
Be gentle with the one who is harsh to you; perhaps he too will soften.
source: Ali ibn Abi Talib, Nahj al-Balagha (counsel to Hasan)
source_display: Ali ibn Abi Talib, Nahj al-Balagha (counsel to Hasan)

text: Whoever consoles a person struck by calamity has a reward like his.
Be patient, as the messengers of firm resolve were patient.
Leave what makes you doubt for what does not make you doubt.
Whoever does evil or wrongs himself, then seeks Allah's forgiveness, will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
Whoever starts a good practice in Islam has its reward and the reward of all who act upon it.
Avoid much suspicion; indeed some suspicion is sin.
If you can do nothing else, refrain from evil; that too is charity for you.
When evening comes, do not wait for morning; when morning comes, do not wait for evening; take from your health for your illness and from your life for your death.
Do not knowingly betray what is entrusted to you.
Look at those below you, not at those above you; that is more fitting so that you do not belittle Allah's blessings.
For whoever fears standing before his Lord there are two gardens.
Hold your tongue, let your home suffice you, and weep over your mistakes.
Hold fast all together to the rope of Allah, and do not be divided.
Successful is the one who accepts Islam, is given sufficient provision and is made content by Allah with what He gave him.
Rebuke your brother by doing him good, and repel his harm by being generous to him.
source: Ali ibn Abi Talib, Nahj al-Balagha
source_display: Ali ibn Abi Talib, Nahj al-Balagha

text: Spread peace, feed others, maintain family ties and pray while people sleep; you will enter Paradise in peace.
Whoever relies on Allah, He is sufficient for him.
True patience is at the first stroke of calamity.
Allah loves those who repent often and those who purify themselves.
You will not believe until you love one another; spread peace among yourselves.
Those who are guided, Allah increases them in guidance and grants them their mindfulness.
Removing something harmful from the road is a charity.
Whoever counts his words among his deeds speaks little.
Tie your camel, then put your trust in Allah.
Indeed, Allah is with the patient.
Whoever reads a letter of the Qur'an earns a good deed, and each good deed is multiplied tenfold.
Put your trust in Allah; Allah suffices as a Guardian.
Do not hate one another, do not envy one another, do not turn away from one another; be brothers, O servants of Allah.

Allah
The One True God
